description: We are Lojain Hana and Yara a student team from Egypt passionate about AI programming and space technology. We combine skills in software development web technologies data and creative problem solving. For NASA Space Apps we aim to create an intuitive health monitoring solution for astronauts that visualizes health data detects unusual patterns and provides timely alerts to support astronaut safety during space missions.
summary:
AstronautCare is an interactive software prototype designed to explore how astronaut health and lower-limb movement can be monitored during space missions. Spaceflight can expose the human body to conditions that affect physical function, making continuous health research and movement assessment important for future exploration.

Our platform combines a 3D interactive human anatomy model, a virtual wearable ankle band, and a real-time sensor dashboard. It visualizes simulated heart rate, blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂), temperature, muscle activity (EMG), ankle angle, and foot pressure. Users can explore anatomical structures, observe movement changes, review sensor trends, and access NASA-related research sources.

By bringing anatomy, movement visualization, and simulated sensor data together, AstronautCare offers an educational environment for understanding astronaut health challenges and exploring future monitoring technologies. It is a research and visualization prototype, not a certified medical device.
details:
The Problem

Human spaceflight presents unique challenges to the human body. Changes in the space environment can affect physical function and movement. Understanding these changes is important for supporting astronaut health and preparing for longer missions.

Our Solution

AstronautCare is an interactive software prototype that brings together three connected elements:

  1. Interactive 3D Human Anatomy: A selectable 3D body model that allows users to explore anatomical structures and understand their functions.
  2. Virtual Astronaut Wearable Band: A conceptual ankle-worn monitoring system represented in the application. It visualizes six simulated measurements: heart rate, SpO₂, temperature, EMG muscle activity, ankle angle, and foot pressure.
  3. Live Monitoring and Research Dashboard: A Flask-based backend receives simulated sensor packets, stores readings, displays real-time charts, and provides access to NASA-related research sources.

How It Works

The browser-based virtual sensor laboratory generates changing readings for different scenarios, including rest, walking, exercise, and recovery. These readings are sent to the backend and displayed on the dashboard. The ankle movement visualization responds to simulated EMG, ankle-angle, and foot-pressure values. Users can also explore anatomy, review historical readings, and export reports.

Technology

  • Python and Flask for the backend
  • JavaScript, HTML, and CSS for the interface
  • Three.js for interactive 3D visualization
  • Chart.js for sensor graphs
  • SQLite for storing sensor history
  • ESP32/Wokwi simulation concept for exploring future hardware integration

Innovation and Impact

AstronautCare connects anatomy education, wearable-sensor concepts, movement visualization, and space-health research in one interactive platform. Instead of displaying isolated numbers, it helps users understand how different measurements relate to movement and human anatomy.

The prototype can serve as a foundation for future research and development of astronaut-health monitoring systems. All current sensor readings are simulated and are not clinical measurements. The platform does not diagnose medical conditions or provide treatment.
